items.original_title: That’s the signal of confidence I like to see: $COHR issues a new $2B share buyback, through open market purchases. Optical industry looks very undervalued right now, especially as it reaches the inflection of the next supercycle. We’re already seeing photonics-SOI substrate players go from $25M revenue -> $1.2B LTAs signed in a quarter. Or $100M backlog -> $500M in a quarter with InP substrates. And we’ll see acceleration for lasers, modules, and the optical supply chain next. I’m sure Coherent finds its own valuation very low now too, especially after signing $20B LTAs recently.

Markets have now given me PTSD on every green rally. That being said, $SOI accelerating from $25m quarterly photonics-SOI revenue… with no forward visibility earlier this year. Into securing $1.2B in agreements this quarter, backed by cash, is extremely transformative and make me happy to see. In terms transcript details: - “AI data center have built large compute power, but some of it remains idle as copper links limit data availability for processing. Optics removes that bottleneck” Reiterating what I said about aggregate capex not applying 1:1 with optical sector, given optical shifts improves GPU utilization - timelines: “Near-package optics brings first volume by the end of the fiscal year, and high volume next year. Co-Packaged Optics for scale out is starting to ramp. TPO for scale up will be the next stage” - “Growth comes in waves, scale out and scale up as a new driver. As those links goes optical, they create new volume on top of today's. In fiscal year 2027, our revenue comes mostly from pluggable transceiver, and we see initial volume from NPO.” - “Growth returned sooner than we had anticipated and with more vigor. Revenue grew 39%, with Photonics-SOI leading the way. Margin expansion has come forward too” - “So, for the capacity reservation agreement we signed, they cover calendar year 2027, calendar year 2028, and beyond” In terms of where they see acceleration: - “Now we see and we believe the new requests that we are getting lately are more for the Co-Packaged Optics and NPO. And especially for the scale-up going forward.” I think that this quarter earnings marks the inflection of optical acceleration for Soitec + silicon photonics. And what it means for a chokepoint to transform into company economics.

Elon Musk predicts 100% of superintelligence compute will be in space, and says Tesla and SpaceX would “probably” be better together: “If you look into the future, orbital compute is really going to be where things scale to.” “In the future, the amount of superintelligence compute that is on Earth will round down to 0% and superintelligence compute in space will round up to 100%.” “Now remember these words, because that sounds like a preposterous thing to say.” “I think superintelligence compute [on Earth] will be less than 0.4% of compute. Therefore, orbital compute will round up to 100%. And I think this is a relatively easy prediction to make, and it’s simply a matter of time before that happens.” Would Tesla and SpaceX be better together? “Probably yes. Now, this is not like let’s merge the companies no matter what. These require shareholder votes, which may or may not succeed, at least in the case of Tesla.” “I can’t just drag them into a non-economic merger that is bad for them, because I’ll obviously get sued.” “It really is just a question of, do SpaceX and Tesla execute better together and create more value than if they’re apart?”

Elon Musk reveals over 30 people now have a Neuralink, some use it to feed themselves with a robot arm, and he's confident it will eventually let people with spinal injuries walk again "Yeah. So Neuralink, by the way, is obviously, as you mentioned, a private company, much, much smaller. I mean, it's just several hundred people. We now have, I think, over 30 people that have received the Neuralink device. So they have a Neuralink in their head." "Our focus initially was giving people who are tetraplegics, quadriplegics, the ability to control their phone or their computer or a robot arm just by thinking. So we call that product Telepathy. So just by thinking, you can control a computer or a robot arm. Some of our customers will literally control a robot arm, and they will actually feed themselves. It gives them the power. I mean, imagine you're tetraplegic. You can't do anything. You can't feed yourself. But now, just by thinking, with the robot arm, you can actually feed yourself with the robot arm." "And how much better… These things that we take for granted are life-changing. And down the road, we feel at this point confident in saying that we'll be able to bridge the signals from the brain, from the motor and sensory cortex, past where the neural damage is from a broken neck or spine, and enable people to walk again."

Elon Musk reveals what really drives him to make humanity a star-faring civilization: “It’s life insurance, but for everything.” “If you simply look at the fossil record and look at how many extinction events have happened, which is a lot, then you know that this is simply a matter of time. It’s a when, not an if.” “It’s important to have insurance for life as a whole. It’s life insurance, but for everything.” But what motivates him even more: “I want to envision a future that’s exciting, that we’re out there exploring new frontiers, going to new star systems, and make science fiction not just fiction forever.” “We should boldly go like Star Trek, boldly go where no one’s gone before. And perhaps we find some long dead alien civilizations, or perhaps we find actual aliens we could talk to.” “You know how you can figure out if something’s really cool about the future? Just ask your kid, and they’ll tell you.” “Life cannot just be about solving one miserable problem after another. There have to be things that excite you and inspire you about the future, that make you happy when you wake up in the morning.” “You can’t wait to see what happens next. And being a star-faring civilization is one of those things.”

Elon Musk reveals how Starlink saved Ukraine from collapse, and sets the record straight on claims he throttled it: “There is no private individual who has helped Ukraine more than I have. I made sure that Starlink was in Ukraine, prepositioned ahead of the Russian invasion.” “When Russia invaded, they disabled all communications, all cell towers, all fiber cables, and every satellite communication system. There was one system they could not disable, and that was Starlink.” “If they had not had Starlink, their entire line would have collapsed because they had no communication system, and Russia would have won. Now, does that sound like a pro-Russian action to you?” “Even to this present day, Starlink provides the backbone of communications for the Ukrainian military and for Ukraine more broadly. If we were to turn off Starlink, the entire Ukrainian front would collapse immediately.” “From the beginning, I said that Starlink is a civilian system. It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government.” “In the Starlink system, there is a speed limit. That speed limit is the speed of the fastest road speed limit in Ukraine, which I think is about 80 miles an hour.” “Do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions that sometimes result in the loss of innocent lives, not just soldiers. That is not my position to do. And yet we’ve been pressed relentlessly to do that, which I think is outrageous.” “Those are the rules that have been in place since the beginning, for years. Now people pressure me to change it, but I’m not changing it.”

Now that we're close to 2027 it's a good idea to stress test downside scenarios where you have: 1. Capex cuts past 2028 2. Stranded Compute / DC Slowdowns 3. Finance deterioration (base case) 4. 2x+ rate hikes Working in parallel and see what happens with valuations of AI longs. If you see acceleration despite all 4, I'd argue that's an opportunity. > Next-gen of photonics is one of the rare segments with an extreme rise in optical content and ASPs that can offset aggregate capex cuts. Everyone’s moving into that space, including Elon Musk doing M&A, Marvell, Samsung and others with M&A… and we haven’t seen economic impact on emerging architectures even hit players from Celestial to Ayar + their suppliers yet. If we look at a scenario where there's excess GPUs but power constraints: We might see slowdown in aggregate accelerator/GPU/ASIC procurement, but your optical engines + light sources + switches players see acceleration. Especially as incentive to replace power inefficient networking... since different (cheap BOM) optical architectures improves GPU utilization or even HBM requirements. So value migrates to players more high-beta to architectural shifts. If Celestial projections are $500m -> $1B, and we expect -30% aggregate capex cuts, I'd argue we'd still see upward revisions from Celestial over the next 2 years. But financing with #3 matters a lot as seen with $AAOI dropping off of a $550M, vs. $COHR getting prepayments for capacity expansion from their customers. Companies that rely on external foundries might be less sensitive to #3 since they're not as capex intensive. On the other hand, companies in sectors have a lot of floating interest like certain Neoclouds, and require further financing might be the most impacted. > Legacy and specialty memory is a different cycle that markets conflate with AI capex. If consumer demand weakens but at the same time, players like Windbond exits DDR2, pricing durability is longer than markets expect. > Wafer/substrate procurement such as ABF, SOI, InP are low cost but large downstream destruction if not secured, so we’ll likely see acceleration here as seen with $NVDA earnings call. > qualification cycle players within bottlenecks remain very compelling, since first revenue in a large TAM, relative to MC is material to that company. If a company is valued at $400m then they get a $200m of orders, it's more asymmetrical to a certain company than a rounding error to a $50B incumbent revenue. _ There’s period of times where prices are dislocated from fundamentals from leveraged players getting wiped. I’d argue that time is now. I disagree with a lot of the stupid "it's over takes" but I agree it's a good idea to haircut future capex expectations and forward valuations due to financing tightening + macro. It's also good idea to see the nuances and stress test downside cases. But TLDR: I'd argue next phase of AI infrastructure is going to be increasingly disconnected from aggregate AI capex growth. I just personally wrote 4 things I'm using to stress test jointly some of the names I'm looking at, so I'm more comfortable waiting things out... despite seeing hedge funds getting liquidated left and right and overwhelming short positioning. I personally see acceleration in more narrow parts of the supply chain, while markets treat the entire AI trade as one. We'll see how things play out on longer horizons.
